description.short: Premium black tea crafted exclusively from buds, sweet and honeyed without smokiness
description.overview: Created as an unsmoked alternative to traditional Lapsang Souchong from the same village of Tongmu, designed for tea connoisseurs seeking refined sweetness without smoke.
description.liquor: Bright golden liquor with copper highlights
description.aroma: Honey, sweet potato, delicate floral notes, subtle fruity acidity
description.taste: Sweet, mellow, without astringency, featuring a honeyed and lightly floral profile
description.aftertaste: Lingering sweet finish with a pleasant "hui gan" sensation in the throat
description.processing: Plucking of buds only → extended withering → rolling → full oxidation → low-temperature drying without smoking

history.origin: Created in 2005 by local tea masters in Tongmu village at the request of merchants seeking a premium unsmoked black tea for the modern market
history.development: Rapidly became one of China's most expensive black teas due to the labor-intensive harvesting of tiny buds and strictly limited production area
history.modern: Today, numerous imitations from other provinces exist under this name; authentic Jin Jun Mei is produced exclusively within the Wuyishan Nature Reserve in Tongmu village
interestingFacts: Producing 500 g of finished tea requires approximately 60,000–80,000 select buds, hand-picked in early spring
Tongmu is the exact village where the world's first black tea, the smoked Lapsang Souchong, was historically invented
